title: docs: two daemon test labels still say the ps1 wrapper records qualityGate verbatim
description:
Found while planning task-42c1e5939d4d4142a8cfbd819f54fa93. That card's DoD limits its diff to the policy.ts hasPassingCheck comment, so these test labels were left out of it.

task-8fc35d31 (completion f1399a3) made scripts/moe-agent.ps1 trim settings.qualityGate where Read-MoeCommitSettings reads it (moe-agent.ps1:2036, `$qg.Trim()`). Both wrappers now run and record the trimmed command. Two test labels still give the old reason:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts:1451, test title 'accepts a pass recorded with a padded qualityGate verbatim, as the PowerShell wrapper records it', and its comment at 1452-1454 ('the ps1 wrapper records it verbatim').
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/deliveryProjection.test.ts:232, case label 'a runner-observed pass of the gate, padded as the ps1 wrapper records it'.

Keep both cases, their fixtures and their assertions. A padded recorded command can still come from three places: records written before task-8fc35d31, an older wrapper that an IDE plugin still bundles, and direct moe.record_check_run callers (state/checkRunStore.ts:106 keeps `command` as sent). Only the stated reason is stale. Labels and comments only; no behaviour change.

Verification trap: run the vitest files in place, but do not run `npm run build` in the shared checkout. Its prebuild regenerates src/generated/initFiles.ts from peers' uncommitted docs/roles edits. See task-42c1e593's plan for the scratch-export recipe.
